newsitem.title: USA: New Haven says wins $8mln in sewer use lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: New Haven says wins $8mln in sewer use lawsuit.

text.p: A Connecticut judge ordered the town of Hamden, Conn., to pay New Haven $8 million in a long standing dispute over unpaid sewer use charges, New Haven Mayor John DeStefano, Jr., said on Thursday.
New Haven Superior Court Judge Beverly J. Hodgson ruled that the town of Hamden has underpaid its share of sewer use charges since 1985.
She ordered Hamden to pay New Haven $8 million in damages, plus interests and costs.
DeStefano said New Haven's court victory was also good for New Haven ratepayers, who have subsidized Hamden's sewer treatment bills for more than a decade.
New Haven's Water Pollution Control Authority system serves some 200,000 customers in New Haven, Hamden, East Haven, North Branford and Woodbridge, Conn.
DeStefano said he took no pleasure in being a party to litigation with a neighboring town, but that Hamden had a legal and ethical responsibility to acknowledge its obligations.
Hamden began taking issue with its share of sewer bills in 1990. When the two municipalities were unable to solve their differences, New Haven filed its lawsuit in 1991.
The case went to trial in February of this year.
